run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: Investigated the app-263-prod-logs index (the only index that exists in the registered Elasticsearch target, 7 documents, all inside the authorized window). No document carries the service value "payment-service"; the service values present are payment-service-us (3 docs), payment-service-eu (2 docs) and payment-service-ap (2 docs), so the exact entity named in the question was not found and the finding is reported against those differently named services. The seven documents hold 4 ERROR, 2 INFO and 1 WARN. payment-service-us logged "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" (07:57:29Z), then "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" (08:57:29Z), then the WARN "Retry queue depth=812" (09:27:29Z). payment-service-eu logged "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" (07:57:29Z) and "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" (08:57:29Z). payment-service-ap logged only INFO "Healthy" lines. Two candidate causes therefore remain open and no single object can be named: a credential problem on the adyen-eu integration of payment-service-eu, and stripe-us upstream timeouts exhausting the 50-connection pool on payment-service-us. The log index contains no message mentioning HTTP 500, so the "500 errors" framing is not directly visible in the supplied documents; ERROR level is the observed signal. Checks needed to confirm rates, latency and call paths failed: every Prometheus query and Jaeger call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and change_history is not integrated, so rates, baselines and configuration-change history are unknown. Separately, in the Kubernetes cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2) there is no app-263 namespace and no payment-service-* workload; the only payment workload is otel-demo/payment (image 2.0.2-payment, 1/1 ready), whose pod restarted at 08:04:13Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown and whose own logs then show successful charge transactions through 09:55:36Z. That restart is a change during the window that I could not place as affected or explained, so it is recorded as a gap and not as impact.

claims.text: The registered Elasticsearch target holds exactly one index, app-263-prod-logs (7 documents, 6.7kb, health green), and its mapping defines the fields level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword) and timestamp (date).

Inside the authorized window the index holds exactly 7 documents spanning 2026-11-22T07:57:29Z to 2026-11-22T09:27:29Z, aggregated as 4 ERROR, 2 INFO and 1 WARN, and by service as payment-service-us=3, payment-service-ap=2, payment-service-eu=2.
No document in app-263-prod-logs carries the service value "payment-service": the service values the aggregation returned are payment-service-us, payment-service-ap and payment-service-eu.

payment-service-us logged ERROR "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" at 2026-11-22T07:57:29Z, ERROR "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" at 2026-11-22T08:57:29Z and WARN "Retry queue depth=812" at 2026-11-22T09:27:29Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" at 2026-11-22T07:57:29Z and ERROR "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" at 2026-11-22T08:57:29Z.

payment-service-ap's only entries are INFO "Healthy: p95 latency 290ms" at 2026-11-22T07:57:29Z and INFO "Healthy" at 2026-11-22T09:27:29Z; the two documents from that service are not error-level. Its absence of errors beyond those two log lines is not established, since the index contains no other telemetry for it.
None of the seven returned message values contains the string "500"; the only upstream HTTP status named in them is 503 (adyen-eu sandbox).

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config declares paymentFailure (variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable (on/off) with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off" for both, so the fault settings visible in that ConfigMap are not switched on.
No ConfigMap in the cluster has a data value matching adyen, stripe or payment-service: 21 ConfigMaps were processed and the filtered selection returned none.

The cluster namespaces are app-102b, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, otel-demo and opspilot-readonly; there is no app-263 namespace, and the only deployments outside system namespaces are app-102b/traffic-manager and the otel-demo workloads (including otel-demo/payment).

Pod otel-demo/payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6) is Running and ready with restartCount 2; its container's last termination has exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z, and the current instance started at 2026-11-22T08:04:20Z.

Deployment otel-demo/payment has observedGeneration 1, replicas 1, ready 1, available 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, with Available and Progressing conditions lastTransitionTime 2026-11-20T16:32–16:33Z, i.e. the pod template was not changed during the incident window.

The current payment container instance in otel-demo logs its startup at 2026-11-22T08:04:22Z ("payment gRPC server started on port 8080") and then only "Charge request received."/"Transaction complete." INFO pairs from 08:05:32Z to 09:55:36Z; the error-filtered sample over 08:57–09:57 contained no error, exception, panic or timeout line.

All 21 events in the window are grouped as app-102b traffic-manager Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod Normal events (ScalingReplicaSet 0→3 at 09:56:13Z, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started) plus two Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint events for app-95/orca (09:21:00Z) and app-162/signup-service (09:32:52Z); no event names a payment pod or payment-service.

For payment-service-eu, the deepest cause the logs support is a credential/configuration fault in its adyen-eu integration: the exact message "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" names an invalid API key, which would make charge attempts fail regardless of adyen-eu availability (adyen-eu had also answered 503 at 07:57:29Z). The value of that key cannot be read here, so the invalidity itself is unverified.

For payment-service-us the sequence suggests the 30s stripe-us call timeout (07:57:29Z) held connections until the 50-connection pool saturated (08:57:29Z) and a retry queue built up (812 at 09:27:29Z), i.e. the dependency stripe-us is the deepest cause; an alternative remains that the max=50 pool and retry policy are undersized for this load. No stripe-us telemetry exists in any available source to separate these.

A common outbound-network fault at 2026-11-22T07:57:29Z is a further candidate, because payment-service-us and payment-service-eu both logged upstream errors in the same second; this is weakened by the two errors naming different providers (stripe-us, adyen-eu), by the absence of any network object or event for it, and by the later eu error being an authentication failure rather than a transport failure.

The otel-demo fault-injection settings paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config were considered as the cause and rejected for this incident: both are declared with defaultVariant "off", and that ConfigMap belongs to otel-demo and targets the otel-demo payment deployment (service.name "payment"), not the payment-service-us/-eu/-ap entities that logged the errors. Runtime flag changes made through flagd would not appear in the ConfigMap, so this rejection is limited to what the ConfigMap shows.
payment-service-ap's entries in the same index are INFO health lines ("Healthy: p95 latency 290ms" and "Healthy"), so the log evidence does not show every payment regional service failing at once.

The only payment workload observable in the Kubernetes cluster, otel-demo/payment (a different entity from payment-service-us/-eu/-ap), served charge requests successfully in its own logs from 08:05:32Z to 09:55:36Z, so its restart did not visibly break charge processing.

Verify and rotate the API credential that payment-service-eu uses for adyen-eu, since its own log states "invalid api_key"; the secret value itself cannot be read in this run, so the check must be done by whoever owns that credential.

Collect stripe-us latency/error data as seen from payment-service-us and review the 50-connection pool and retry-queue settings, because a 30s upstream timeout followed by pool exhaustion and a retry backlog of 812 is the observed sequence; no latency baseline exists in this run to prove a degradation trend.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access for the target so the reported HTTP 500 rate, per-dependency spans and any latency baseline can be measured; every metrics and traces call in this run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable: metrics_range_query, get_label_values (service_name and k8s_cluster_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total / kube_* series) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so payment error ratios, HTTP 500 counts, latency readings and any comparable baseline are unknown rather than zero.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_search for service "payment" and traces_list_services both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level call path or error-span evidence exists for this incident.

The exact service name in the question, "payment-service", does not exist as a service value in app-263-prod-logs; only payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap appear, and none of the seven messages mentions HTTP 500 explicitly.

No Kubernetes object for payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap exists in the cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2): there is no app-263 namespace and the only payment workload is otel-demo/payment, so workload status and pod events for the failing services are unknown.

No document or tool result carries a cluster, region or environment field for app-263-prod-logs, so the index cannot be attributed to a named cluster; the Kubernetes facts cited come only from the cluster reachable here (production-eu-west-2) and describe otel-demo, a different service identity.
The adyen-eu api_key value cannot be verified because secrets are unreadable, so the claim that the credential is invalid rests on the application's own log text alone.

The otel-demo/payment pod restarted at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown while its pod template stayed unchanged (observedGeneration 1); its previous container instance produced 0 log lines and no pod event names it, so what triggered the restart is unknown and is not placed as impact or cause.

Runtime fault-flag state held by flagd (SetFlag changes not reflected in ConfigMap flagd-config) is not observable, so an injected payment fault cannot be fully excluded even though the ConfigMap shows defaultVariant "off".
stripe-us and adyen-eu are external processors with no logs, metrics or traces in any available source, so neither dependency's own behaviour can be confirmed.

The change_history integration is not configured in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change history for the app-263 services could be checked; the 4MiB/time limits did not truncate any cited result.
next_steps: Have the payment-service-eu owner validate and rotate the adyen-eu API key referenced as "invalid api_key".
Pull stripe-us latency/error telemetry from the payment-service-us side and review its connection-pool max (50) and retry-queue configuration.
Restore or re-register the Prometheus and Jaeger targets for m0-otel-20260909 so error-rate, latency-baseline and span-level confirmation can be attempted.
Confirm whether the app-263 environment is intentionally out of scope of the reachable Kubernetes cluster, and if not, provide access to the cluster that hosts payment-service-us/-eu/-ap.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:

  scrape_timeout: 10s

otlp:

    promote_resource_attributes:

    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace

    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name

  scheme: https

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
